gaps.sentence: We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: It took me ages ___ used to the new keyboard.
gaps.explanation: it takes time + to-infinitive: took me ages to get used to the keyboard.

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)
avoid is followed by -ing: avoid talking.

gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).
deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: We're thinking of ___ to the coast for the weekend.
They accused me of ___ the rules.
